title: OpenAPI security scheme declarations without a credential value
summary: A synthetic OpenAPI 3.1 document whose components.securitySchemes declare an apiKey (header name api-key), HTTP Basic, HTTP Bearer with bearerFormat JWT, OAuth 2.0 client credentials and OpenID Connect, with a root security requirement that names the schemes, and no credential value anywhere.
rationale: The document is full of credential vocabulary: apiKey, api-key, bearer, bearerFormat: JWT, tokenUrl, security requirements that name a scheme. Every one of those spans is a field name, a scheme name, a header name or a URL that the specification defines as part of the declaration; the Security Scheme Object has no field that carries the value a client sends, and the guide says onboarding and key exchange are outside OpenAPI. Reporting the declaration punishes documenting authentication, and masking the header name or scheme name would destroy the description a reader needs. Where an example slot carries an actual literal is a separate question, left to the example cases.

expectation.rationale: Unresolved as an expectation; the structural facts are settled. The specification defines apiKey name as the name of the header, query or cookie parameter, http scheme as the name of the Authorization scheme, and bearerFormat as a documentation hint about how a bearer token is formatted; a security requirement names a declared scheme and lists scopes; no fixed field of the object is defined to hold a credential value, and the OpenAPI Initiative's guide says deployment information such as onboarding or key exchange is out of scope. That describes the roles of the fields; it does not state that a declaration is not sensitive or how a reader should treat it, and the repository's standards rule (ADR 0019) keeps a role description read as non-secrecy at project-policy. Candidate outcome, recommended for a maintainer decision (project-policy with a non-author reviewer): must-not-flag for the declaration text. Planned fixture, not built because an assertable fixture needs the decision: the Learn guide's five declarations (apiKey header api-key, Basic, Bearer with bearerFormat JWT, OAuth 2.0 client credentials with example.com token URL, OpenID Connect with a discovery URL) plus a root security requirement, with no credential value. Precondition: the input is the declaration text as written; no document is resolved or fetched.

sources.supports: Security Scheme Object fixed fields: type, description, name (apiKey: the name of the header, query or cookie parameter to be used), in, scheme (http: the name of the HTTP Authentication scheme to be used in the Authorization header), bearerFormat (a hint to the client to identify how the bearer token is formatted; primarily for documentation purposes), flows, openIdConnectUrl (well-known URL to discover the provider metadata).
A Security Requirement Object property name must correspond to a security scheme declared under the Components Object; for oauth2 and openIdConnect the value is a list of scope names.
OpenAPI provides enough information to give humans and tooling the means to understand the basic security requirements, but deployment information such as onboarding or key exchange is out-of-scope.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. Authored from the cited pages read on 2026-10-04, before any scanner was consulted. The OpenAPI Specification is a standard with no issuing provider; it is cited only for its own text, never for what any provider issues. Reference resolution, example generation, request-sample generation and masking are tool behaviors owned downstream (credential-eval, #150); no scanner or adapter capability is assumed.
